text:
alex: Quick heads-up — ran a cross-GPU attention sweep (A100 / H100 / L40S) for seq lens [32,64,128,256,512] x batch sizes [1,2,4,8]. KV-cache toggled on/off, warm vs cold. Posting the short summary.

ben: Nice, curious about which kernel mix dominated.

alex: TL;DR numbers (median p50 latency tokens/ms), warm KV cache:
```
A100  : seq32 bsz8 -> flash_v2  2.4k toks/s, paged_fused 1.9k
H100  : seq128 bsz4 -> flash_v2 1.6k, hybrid_tile 1.5k
L40S  : seq256 bsz2 -> paged_fused 800, flash_v2 720
cold KV -> add ~18-35% latency depending on seq*bsz
```
Full CSV uploaded to CI artifact: https://ci.redwood/internal/artifacts/3850123456/attn-sweep.csv

maria: That cold KV hit looks high — did you see eviction churn during the run?

alex: Yep. On L40S at seq256 bsz2 we got repeated KV evict/refill bursts when the kernel switched to paged_fused. Trace excerpt: `TRACE: step=842 kernel=paged_fused kv_evictions=12 refill_ms=24`

cheng: Can you paste the kernel selector trace? I want to see the exact heuristic boundary that flipped.

alex: Selector log (abridged):
```
# heuristics eval
if seq_len >= 192 and bsz <= 4 -> prefer paged_fused
elif seq_len * bsz >= 2048 -> prefer hybrid_tile
else -> flash_v2
```
It flipped to paged_fused for seq256 bsz2 because of the first rule.

anya: Suggestion: change rule to require `seq_len >= 256 AND bsz <= 2 AND kv_warm == true` before paged_fused. The current rule doesn't account for KV coldness.

ben: Did you run a sequential microburst test? i.e., 1-request spikes that break batching assumptions. Those cause suboptimal kernel picks if selector uses recent latency only.

alex: I did a microburst run. With small bursts (5 requests in 200ms window) the batcher gave up and selector fell back to lower-latency but lower-throughput kernels, which increased p95 by ~40ms on H100 for seq64. Logged sample: `BATCHER: timeout=15ms -> flush`

perf-bot: CI run 3850123456 finished — perf-regression alert flagged for L40S seq256 bsz2 (regression +12% vs baseline). Link: https://ci.redwood/internal/runs/3850123456

cheng: For immediate mitigation, can we: 1) tighten the selector hysteresis to require 3 consecutive evals before switching; 2) prefer flash_v2 when KV coldness flag is detected; 3) cap prefetch window to avoid heavy evictions. Small changes should avoid oscillation.

alex: Agreed. Quick notes from profiling: `nvprof` slices show memcpy spikes aligning with refills, not kernel compute. So the real cost is memory churn, not arithmetic.

anya: I'll open a PR with the heuristic tweak and a feature flag for canary on dedicated. We should also add a KV-warmness metric to the console so customers can see when they're hitting the cold path.

ben: Can someone create a minimal repro script we can run on staging (A100)? I can validate.

alex: Created: `perf/run_attn_sweep.sh --gpus A100,H100,L40S --kv-toggle --microburst` and uploaded to /staging/scripts. Will add instructions in the PR.

maria: Thanks — tagging @infra for possible prefetch rate-limits at the driver level if needed.

cheng: Follow-ups:
- [ ] PR heuristic update (anya)
- [ ] Staging repro run (ben + alex)
- [ ] Add KV-warmness metric to console (product/monitoring)
- [ ] Postmortem if regression persists after canary

alex: On it. Will roll canary tomorrow early AM. :thumbsup:
